The test image shows a corn leaf with a large, elongated tan/grayish-brown lesion that is cigar/spindle-shaped, running parallel to the leaf veins. The lesion has a pale tan center. Top candidates: Northern Leaf Blight (large cigar-shaped lesions) or Gray Leaf Spot (rectangular tan lesions bounded by veins).

Now viewing reference images — one per candidate class first.
Strong match to Northern Leaf Blight — large, elongated cigar-shaped tan lesions. Now checking Gray Leaf Spot.
That Gray Leaf Spot reference is a whole-field view — not useful for lesion comparison. Let me check Southern Corn Leaf Blight and one more Gray Leaf Spot.
Gray Leaf Spot shows smaller, rectangular vein-bounded lesions — different from the test. Northern Leaf Blight remains the top candidate. Using my final view on Southern Corn Leaf Blight.

Southern Corn Leaf Blight reference shows ear/stalk symptoms — not a leaf lesion match.

**Summary:**
- Test image: large, elongated, cigar/spindle-shaped tan-brown lesion on corn leaf, running parallel to veins — classic Northern Leaf Blight morphology
- NLB reference confirmed identical lesion shape and color
- Gray Leaf Spot: smaller, rectangular, vein-bounded lesions — doesn't match
- Southern Corn Leaf Blight: different presentation entirely
